content.text:
`python3 -m unittest -q` now passes all 7 tests. I fixed two bugs in `household/bills.py` and changed one test that was wrong.

1. **`split_bill` dropped the leftover cents.** It returned `total // people` for every person, so 1001 split two ways gave `[500, 500]` and a cent was lost. It now uses `divmod` and gives one extra cent to each of the first few people, as the docstring says. 1001 split two ways is now `[501, 500]`.

2. **`due_dates` failed when the dates crossed into a new year.** It added to the month number without ever moving to the next year, so it asked for month 13 and crashed. It now works out the year and month together with `divmod`, so Dec 2026 is followed by Jan 2027.

3. **I changed one test, `test_three_ways`, and you should know about it.** It expected `split_bill(1000, 3)` to return `[333, 333, 333]`. That only adds up to 999, which goes against the function's own docstring ("the shares add up to exactly total_cents"). The test was only passing because of the first bug. I changed the expected result to `[334, 333, 333]`. If losing the leftover cent was actually what you wanted, tell me and I'll revert this and update the docstring instead. I don't think that's likely.

I haven't committed anything.
